verdicts.reason: The quote 'Yea I agree drop it.' is line 5 of the file, the owner's first blockquote. What 'it' is comes from the file around the quote, not the quote: the preamble (line 3) names design questions 13 and 10, decided item 1 (lines 20 to 23) is design question 13 and the context paragraph (lines 11 to 12) says the row's three criteria change only what a screen reader hears. The statement follows from the file, so it holds; the identification of the referent makes it closer to inferred than verbatim, which reconcile should know when it weighs the confidence.

The quote runs across lines 8 and 9 of the second blockquote, verbatim once the '> ' prefixes and the line break are removed: 'but yea / the address earch aint something we need to build yet'. The statement says no more than the quote. The ref says lines 7 to 9 where 8 to 9 would be exact, which is a loose ref, not a refutation.
The quote is the opening of line 7, word for word: 'The shout on address search is it's not a "get done for our deadline job"'. The statement restates it in plain English and adds nothing.

The quote spans lines 7 and 8 verbatim ('some of the stuff in dr 2.1 (like / templates) is concept work'). The quote gives templates as the instance of the concept work it names, so the statement follows.

The quote is on line 8, verbatim. The quote's subject is 'some of the stuff in dr 2.1', so 'Design Release 2.1 mixes concept work in with the work that has to be done for the deadline' is a fair reading of the same words, and 'making things confusing' is in the quote.

The quote is the whole second blockquote, lines 7 to 9, verbatim once the prefixes and line breaks are removed. The inference is sound and the statement says why: the same two sentences put address search outside the 'get done for our deadline job' and name concept work as what is mixed into the 'get this done work', so address search sits on the concept-work side. The note is right that the owner's own words name only templates as concept work, so inferred is the correct confidence.

The quote is the opening of decided item 1, line 20, verbatim: '**The country search keeps the accessible autocomplete's own announcements.** Design question 13.' The inference is sound and the statement says why: the agreed drop leaves the component's own announcements as the behaviour, with nothing added. Inferred is right, since naming the accessible autocomplete is the main session's reading rather than the owner's words.

The quote is decided item 1, lines 20 to 22, verbatim once the list indentation and line breaks are removed. The statement takes only the label half of it, so it does not overreach, and the note is right that the owner's own words are only 'Yea I agree drop it.'
Same quote as claim 008, decided item 1, lines 20 to 22. The statement takes only the 'Selected <country>' half of it. Sound, and inferred is the right confidence for the same reason.

The quote 'on the live animals, germinal products or high-risk plants origin pages' spans lines 21 and 22 verbatim. The source's 'or' inside a negative ('No ... label and no ... announcement, on the live animals, germinal products or high-risk plants origin pages') covers all three pages, so reading it as all three is sound.

The quote 'inc-189 is dropped and req-020 is out of scope.' is on line 22, verbatim. The statement takes the first half only. Inferred is right: the increment disposition is the main session's reading of the owner's agreement to drop.
Same quote as claim 011, line 22. The statement takes the second half only and adds nothing.

The quote 'The question no longer goes to the designer.' spans lines 22 and 23 verbatim. 'The question' is decided item 1's own question, named on line 20 as design question 13, so naming it 13 in the statement is sound.

The quote 'The add-address pages keep every field shown from the start, as main has them.' spans lines 24 and 25 verbatim. The statement's added 'rather than offering an address search first' follows from decided item 2's own subject, address search parked, so it does not overreach. The quote spans lines 25 and 26 verbatim ('inc-194 is deferred and its requirements stay / adopted but parked, so the question does not go to the designer now.'). The statement takes the first clause only.

Same quote as claim 015, lines 25 to 26. The statement takes 'its requirements stay adopted but parked', and the note's reasoning from 'aint something we need to build yet' — not yet, rather than never — is sound.
The quote 'so the question does not go to the designer now' is on line 26, verbatim. 'The question' is decided item 2's own question, named on line 24 as design question 10, so naming it 10 is sound.

The quote spans lines 28 and 29 of decided item 3, verbatim including the trailing semicolon. The statement restates it and names no actor beyond 'someone', which the source's bare imperative 'ask' supports. Inferred is right: the owner states the confusion, not the rule.

The quote spans lines 29 and 30 verbatim ('a feature main does not have at all, shown only in the prototype, is the usual sign / of concept work'). The statement adds only that main is the real service's main branch, which the file's context paragraph (line 15) supports.

The quote 'Flag it to Sam rather than build it.' is the last sentence of line 30, verbatim. The statement's 'A row judged to be concept work' is the 'it' decided item 3 has been talking about since line 28, so the reading is sound.

The file is not silent where this gap says it is. The context paragraph (lines 11 to 12) calls the Welsh versions one of 'The row's three criteria', and decided item 1 (line 22) disposes of the whole row: 'inc-189 is dropped and req-020 is out of scope.' Dropping the increment and putting the requirement out of scope carries all three criteria with it, and the Welsh versions are translations of the two announcements the same item says are not built, so there is nothing left to translate. Nothing is left open for reconcile to chase.

I looked at the second blockquote (lines 7 to 8) and decided item 3 (lines 27 to 30) and the file is indeed silent there: templates are called concept work and nothing more. No decided item gives templates a disposition, and no increment or requirement id is named for them, unlike inc-189, req-020 and inc-194. Decided item 3's standing rule would apply to a templates row, but it decides nothing about the templates work itself, so the open point stands. The empty quote is correct for a gap.

I looked at line 9 and decided item 2 (lines 24 to 26) and the file is indeed silent there: 'aint something we need to build yet' and 'inc-194 is deferred and its requirements stay adopted but parked' say the work is parked and no more. No owner, trigger or date for unparking it appears anywhere in the file. The empty quote is correct for a gap.
